For he who thinks fit to give food to people while they are still panting, when the body is full of many vapours, will want also to fill them up all the more by the drinking of hot wine.
But since the very hot, much like the cold, naturally contracts and braces the stomach, he guards against doing this.
But also to eat once a day, to abstain from bathing, to sleep on a hard bed, and to walk about naked, as far as may be possible.

beads.greek: [196] Κάλλιον ἂν ἦν εἰρῆσθαι πρὸς αὐτῷ μὴ μονοσιτέειν, ἀλλ᾿ ὀλιγοσιτεῖν.
beads.english: [196] It would have been better to have said at this point (πρὸς αὐτῷ) not 'to eat once a day' but 'to eat little'.

beads.greek: ἔνιοι γὰρ τῶν μονοσιτούντων πολὺ πλείω προσφέρονται τῶν δὶς σιτουμένων.
beads.english: For some of those who eat once a day take in much more than those who eat twice.

beads.greek: ὥσπερ δὲ τὸ λουτρὸν ἐκθερμαῖνον τὸ σῶμα καὶ μάλιστα τοὐκτὸς, εἰς ἀνάδοσίν τε τροφῆς καὶ πρόσθεσιν τῶν ἀναδοθέντων συντελεῖ, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον ἡ ἀλουσία τοῖς ἐναντίοις συναίρεται.
beads.english: Just as the bath, by heating the body through, and especially its exterior, contributes to the distribution of nourishment and to the apposition of what has been distributed, by the same reasoning abstention from bathing assists the opposite effects.

beads.greek: καὶ ἡ σκληροκοιτία δὲ λυπεῖ καὶ συνέχει καὶ σφίγγει τὸ σῶμα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν εἰς πᾶν μέρος ἐπίδοσιν αὐτοῦ κω- λύει.
beads.english: Sleeping on a hard bed also distresses, constricts and binds the body, and for this reason prevents its growth into every part.

beads.greek: κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον καὶ τὸ γυμνὸν περιπατεῖν ψύχει μὲν ἅπαντα τὰ μετὰ τὸ δέρμα μόρια. συνελαύνει δὲ εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα τὴν θερμασίαν, ὡς πέττε- σθαι μὲν καλῶς τὰ σιτία, τὴν δὲ πάντη φορὰν αὐτῶν κω- λύειν.
beads.english: By the same reasoning, walking about naked cools all the parts beneath the skin and drives the warmth together into the depth and the viscera, so that the foods are concocted well but their conveyance in every direction is prevented.

beads.greek: Ὁκόσοι δὲ βούλονται λεπτοὶ ἐόντες παχύτεροι γενέσθαι, τά τε ἅλλα ποιέειν τἀναντία ἐκείνοισι οἶσιν ἔφην καὶ νῆστιν μηδεμίην ταλαιπωρίην ποιέεσθαι.
beads.english: Those who, being thin, wish to become fatter should do the other things opposite to those I have mentioned, and should undertake no exertion while fasting.

greek_sentences: [196] Κάλλιον ἂν ἦν εἰρῆσθαι πρὸς αὐτῷ μὴ μονοσιτέειν, ἀλλ᾿ ὀλιγοσιτεῖν.
ἔνιοι γὰρ τῶν μονοσιτούντων πολὺ πλείω προσφέρονται τῶν δὶς σιτουμένων.
ὥσπερ δὲ τὸ λουτρὸν ἐκθερμαῖνον τὸ σῶμα καὶ μάλιστα τοὐκτὸς, εἰς ἀνάδοσίν τε τροφῆς καὶ πρόσθεσιν τῶν ἀναδοθέντων συντελεῖ, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον ἡ ἀλουσία τοῖς ἐναντίοις συναίρεται.
καὶ ἡ σκληροκοιτία δὲ λυπεῖ καὶ συνέχει καὶ σφίγγει τὸ σῶμα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν εἰς πᾶν μέρος ἐπίδοσιν αὐτοῦ κω- λύει.
κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον καὶ τὸ γυμνὸν περιπατεῖν ψύχει μὲν ἅπαντα τὰ μετὰ τὸ δέρμα μόρια.
συνελαύνει δὲ εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα τὴν θερμασίαν, ὡς πέττε- σθαι μὲν καλῶς τὰ σιτία, τὴν δὲ πάντη φορὰν αὐτῶν κω- λύειν.
Ὁκόσοι δὲ βούλονται λεπτοὶ ἐόντες παχύτεροι γενέσθαι, τά τε ἅλλα ποιέειν τἀναντία ἐκείνοισι οἶσιν ἔφην καὶ νῆστιν μηδεμίην ταλαιπωρίην ποιέεσθαι.
english_sentences: [196] It would have been better to have said at this point (πρὸς αὐτῷ) not 'to eat once a day' but 'to eat little'.
For some of those who eat once a day take in much more than those who eat twice.

Just as the bath, by heating the body through, and especially its exterior, contributes to the distribution of nourishment and to the apposition of what has been distributed, by the same reasoning abstention from bathing assists the opposite effects.
Sleeping on a hard bed also distresses, constricts and binds the body, and for this reason prevents its growth into every part.

By the same reasoning, walking about naked cools all the parts beneath the skin and drives the warmth together into the depth and the viscera, so that the foods are concocted well but their conveyance in every direction is prevented.
Those who, being thin, wish to become fatter should do the other things opposite to those I have mentioned, and should undertake no exertion while fasting.

beads.greek: [197] Τἀναντία τῶν εἰρημένων τοῖς παχέσιν ἐστὶ τὸ μήτε ἀσθμαίνοντας ἐπιχειρεῖν τοῖς σιτίοις, ἀλλ᾿ ὅταν ἤδη κατὰ φύσιν ἀναπνέωσι, μήτε μονοσιτεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ ἤτοι δὶς ἐσθίειν ἢ καὶ τρίς.
beads.english: [197] The opposite of what was said for the stout is neither to set about one's food while panting, but only when they are already breathing in accordance with nature, nor to eat once a day, but to eat either twice or even three times.

beads.greek: οὕτω δὲ καὶ ταῖς ἀλουσίαις τἀναντία ποιῶν λού- σεται δὶς, ἐξ ἅπαντος μὲν ἐπὶ τροφῇ χρόνου τὸ δεύτερον λουτρὸν περιλαμβάνων, ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε δὲ καὶ τὸ πρῶτον.
beads.english: So too, doing the opposite of going without baths, he will bathe twice, in any case placing the second bath before food, and sometimes the first as well.

beads.greek: οὕτω δὲ καὶ τὰ γυμνάσια βραχέα τε γυμνάσεται καὶ βραδέα καὶ μετὰ τροφήν.
beads.english: So too he will perform his exercises short and slow, and after food.

beads.greek: κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον καὶ τὸ μαλακῶς κοιμᾶσθαι καὶ μὴ γυμνὸν ὁμιλεῖν τῷ περιέχοντι, τούτοις ἐστὶ χρήσιμον.
beads.english: On the same reasoning, sleeping softly and not being in contact with the surrounding air naked are useful for these people.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτο γοῦν καὶ αἱ γυμνασταὶ τὰ μὲν μετὰ τοῦ προσάπτεσθαι καὶ σωματομαχεῖν, οὕτω γὰρ ὀνο- μάζουσιν αὐτοί τινα γινόμενα γυμνάσια, περιλαμβάνουσιν, ἐφ᾿ ὦν σαρκῶσαι θέλουσι, φυλαττόμενοι γυμνοὺς γυμνάζειν αὐτοὺς τὸ σῶμα καὶ μὴ μετὰ συμπλοκῆς.
beads.english: For this reason, at any rate, the trainers include the exercises done with laying hold and body-fighting (for that is what they themselves call certain exercises that are performed) for those on whom they wish to put flesh, taking care not to exercise them with the body naked, and not with grappling.

beads.greek: ἔμπαλιν δὲ ὅσους λεπτῦναι βούλονται, μετὰ τοῦ ταχέος γυμνασίου καὶ χωρὶς τῆς πρώτης συμπλοκῆς γυμνάζουσιν.
beads.english: Conversely, those whom they wish to make thin they exercise with rapid exercise and without the first grappling.

greek_sentences: [197] Τἀναντία τῶν εἰρημένων τοῖς παχέσιν ἐστὶ τὸ μήτε ἀσθμαίνοντας ἐπιχειρεῖν τοῖς σιτίοις, ἀλλ᾿ ὅταν ἤδη κατὰ φύσιν ἀναπνέωσι, μήτε μονοσιτεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ ἤτοι δὶς ἐσθίειν ἢ καὶ τρίς.
οὕτω δὲ καὶ ταῖς ἀλουσίαις τἀναντία ποιῶν λού- σεται δὶς, ἐξ ἅπαντος μὲν ἐπὶ τροφῇ χρόνου τὸ δεύτερον λουτρὸν περιλαμβάνων, ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε δὲ καὶ τὸ πρῶτον.
οὕτω δὲ καὶ τὰ γυμνάσια βραχέα τε γυμνάσεται καὶ βραδέα καὶ μετὰ τροφήν.
κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον καὶ τὸ μαλακῶς κοιμᾶσθαι καὶ μὴ γυμνὸν ὁμιλεῖν τῷ περιέχοντι, τούτοις ἐστὶ χρήσιμον.

διὰ τοῦτο γοῦν καὶ αἱ γυμνασταὶ τὰ μὲν μετὰ τοῦ προσάπτεσθαι καὶ σωματομαχεῖν, οὕτω γὰρ ὀνο- μάζουσιν αὐτοί τινα γινόμενα γυμνάσια, περιλαμβάνουσιν, ἐφ᾿ ὦν σαρκῶσαι θέλουσι, φυλαττόμενοι γυμνοὺς γυμνάζειν αὐτοὺς τὸ σῶμα καὶ μὴ μετὰ συμπλοκῆς.
ἔμπαλιν δὲ ὅσους λεπτῦναι βούλονται, μετὰ τοῦ ταχέος γυμνασίου καὶ χωρὶς τῆς πρώτης συμπλοκῆς γυμνάζουσιν.
english_sentences: [197] The opposite of what was said for the stout is neither to set about one's food while panting, but only when they are already breathing in accordance with nature, nor to eat once a day, but to eat either twice or even three times.
So too, doing the opposite of going without baths, he will bathe twice, in any case placing the second bath before food, and sometimes the first as well.
So too he will perform his exercises short and slow, and after food.
On the same reasoning, sleeping softly and not being in contact with the surrounding air naked are useful for these people.

For this reason, at any rate, the trainers include the exercises done with laying hold and body-fighting (for that is what they themselves call certain exercises that are performed) for those on whom they wish to put flesh, taking care not to exercise them with the body naked, and not with grappling.
Conversely, those whom they wish to make thin they exercise with rapid exercise and without the first grappling.

beads.greek: Τοῖσι δὲ ἐμέτοισι χρὴ καὶ τοῖσι κατακλύσμασι τοῖσι τῆς [198] κοιλίης, ᾧδε χρέεσθαι ἓξ μῆνας τοὺς χειμερινοὺς ἐμέειν· οὗτος γὰρ ὁ χρόνος φλεγματωδέστερος τοῦ θερινοῦ καὶ τὰ νουσήματα γίνεται περὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ περὶ τὸ χω- ρίον τοῦτο τὸ ὑπὲρ τῶν φρενῶν.
beads.english: "One should use vomitings and clysters of the [198] belly as follows: vomit during the six winter months, for this period is more phlegmatic than the summer, and the diseases arise about the head and about this region above the diaphragm.

beads.greek: ὅταν δὲ ᾖ τὸ θάλπος, τοῖσι κατακλύσμασι χρέεσθαι.
beads.english: But when there is the heat, use clysters.

beads.greek: ἡ γὰρ ὥρη καυματώδης καὶ χολωδέστερόν ἐστι τὸ σῶμα καὶ αἱ βαρύτητες ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ καὶ ἐν τοῖσι γούνασι καὶ θερμὰ γίνονται καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ στρόφοι γίνονται. δεῖ οὖν τὸ σῶμα ψύχειν καὶ τὰ μετεωριζόμενα κάτω ὑπάγειν ἀπὸ τῶν χωρίων τουτέων.
beads.english: For the season is burning, and the body is more bilious, and heavinesses occur in the loins and in the knees, and heats arise, and gripings occur in the belly.

beads.greek: Τίνα καλεῖ κατακλύσματα διὰ τῶν ἐφεξῆς ἐδήλωσεν αὐτός. τά τε ἀπὸ τῶν γαλάκτων εἰπὼν καὶ τὸ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρεβίνθων ἑψημένον ὕδωρ ἅλμην τε καὶ θάλασσαν.
beads.english: One must therefore cool the body and draw downward, away from these regions, the matters that are rising upward." What he calls clysters (kataklysmata) he has himself made clear in what follows, mentioning those made from milks, and the water in which chickpeas have been boiled, and brine and sea water.

beads.greek: ἕτερα γάρ ἐστι τούτων τὰ καθαίροντα φάρμακα κενωτικὰ τοῦ παν- τὸς σώματος ὄντα.
beads.english: For the purging drugs, which are evacuant of the whole body, are something different from these.

greek_sentences: Τοῖσι δὲ ἐμέτοισι χρὴ καὶ τοῖσι κατακλύσμασι τοῖσι τῆς [198] κοιλίης, ᾧδε χρέεσθαι ἓξ μῆνας τοὺς χειμερινοὺς ἐμέειν· οὗτος γὰρ ὁ χρόνος φλεγματωδέστερος τοῦ θερινοῦ καὶ τὰ νουσήματα γίνεται περὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ περὶ τὸ χω- ρίον τοῦτο τὸ ὑπὲρ τῶν φρενῶν.
ὅταν δὲ ᾖ τὸ θάλπος, τοῖσι κατακλύσμασι χρέεσθαι.
ἡ γὰρ ὥρη καυματώδης καὶ χολωδέστερόν ἐστι τὸ σῶμα καὶ αἱ βαρύτητες ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ καὶ ἐν τοῖσι γούνασι καὶ θερμὰ γίνονται καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ στρόφοι γίνονται.
δεῖ οὖν τὸ σῶμα ψύχειν καὶ τὰ μετεωριζόμενα κάτω ὑπάγειν ἀπὸ τῶν χωρίων τουτέων.
Τίνα καλεῖ κατακλύσματα διὰ τῶν ἐφεξῆς ἐδήλωσεν αὐτός.
τά τε ἀπὸ τῶν γαλάκτων εἰπὼν καὶ τὸ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρεβίνθων ἑψημένον ὕδωρ ἅλμην τε καὶ θάλασσαν.
ἕτερα γάρ ἐστι τούτων τὰ καθαίροντα φάρμακα κενωτικὰ τοῦ παν- τὸς σώματος ὄντα.
english_sentences: "One should use vomitings and clysters of the [198] belly as follows: vomit during the six winter months, for this period is more phlegmatic than the summer, and the diseases arise about the head and about this region above the diaphragm.
But when there is the heat, use clysters.
For the season is burning, and the body is more bilious, and heavinesses occur in the loins and in the knees, and heats arise, and gripings occur in the belly.

One must therefore cool the body and draw downward, away from these regions, the matters that are rising upward." What he calls clysters (kataklysmata) he has himself made clear in what follows, mentioning those made from milks, and the water in which chickpeas have been boiled, and brine and sea water.
For the purging drugs, which are evacuant of the whole body, are something different from these.

beads.greek: ὥσπερ οὖν τὰ βαλανεῖα κατακλύζειν οἱ βαλανεῖς λέγουσι, τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς λίθων ἀποπλύνοντες τὸν πηλὸν καὶ τὸν ῥύπον, οὕτω καὶ τὰ τῆς γαστρός τε καὶ τῶν [199] ἐντέρων κατακλύσματα, περιπλύνει τὸ φλέγμα καὶ τὴν χο- λὴν αὐτῶν.
beads.english: Just as, then, the bath-keepers say that they 'flush out' (κατακλύζειν) the baths when they wash off the mud and the dirt from the stones in them, so too the flushings (κατακλύσματα) of the stomach and of the [199] intestines wash away the phlegm and the bile from them.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἐν τῷ χειμῶνι φλέγμα γεννᾶται κατὰ τὴν κοιλίαν, ἐκκενοῦν αὐτὸ διὰ τῶν ἐμέτων συμβου- λεύει. τοῦ θέρους δὲ τὴν ἐπιπολάζουσαν ἄνω χολὴν ἀντι- σπᾷν κάτω.
beads.english: Since, then, in winter phlegm is generated in the belly, he advises evacuating it by means of vomitings; but in summer, drawing the bile that floats up on top back downwards.

beads.greek: καθαίρειν μέντοι τὸ σύμπαν σῶμα βουληθέν- τι σοι θέρους μὲν διὰ τῆς ἄνω, χειμῶνος δὲ διὰ τῆς κά- τω κοιλίας φαρμακευτέον, ὡς ἐν ἀφορισμοῖς εἴρηται.
beads.english: If, however, you wish to purge the whole body, you must administer drugs in summer through the upper belly, and in winter through the lower belly, as has been said in the Aphorisms.

beads.greek: τὰ μὲν γὰρ ἤδη πλεονάζοντα ἡ κάθαρσις ἰᾶται διὰ τῶν χω- ρίων ᾗ ῥέπει τὴν κάθαρσιν ποιούμενος. ἀκτέα γὰρ ᾗ ῥέπει διὰ τῶν συμφερόντων χωρίων.
beads.english: For purging cures what is already in excess when one performs the purging through the regions toward which it inclines; for one must lead it where it inclines, through the appropriate regions.

beads.greek: ὅσα δὲ κωλῦσαι θέλεις αὐξη- θῆναι, διὰ τῶν ἀντικειμένων χωρίων ἀντισπᾷν προσήκει.
beads.english: But whatever you wish to prevent from increasing, it is fitting to draw off in the opposite direction through the opposite regions.

beads.greek: Ἔστω δὲ τὰ κατακλύσματα τοῖσιν μὲν παχυτέροισι καὶ ὑγροτέροισιν ἁλμυρώτερα καὶ λεπτότερα, τοῖσι δὲ ξηρο- τέροισι καὶ προσεσταλμένοισι καὶ ἀσθενεστέροισι λιπαρώτερα καὶ παχύτερα.
beads.english: Let the flushings be saltier and thinner for those who are stouter and moister, and fattier and thicker for those who are drier, contracted and weaker.

greek_sentences: ὥσπερ οὖν τὰ βαλανεῖα κατακλύζειν οἱ βαλανεῖς λέγουσι, τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς λίθων ἀποπλύνοντες τὸν πηλὸν καὶ τὸν ῥύπον, οὕτω καὶ τὰ τῆς γαστρός τε καὶ τῶν [199] ἐντέρων κατακλύσματα, περιπλύνει τὸ φλέγμα καὶ τὴν χο- λὴν αὐτῶν.
ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἐν τῷ χειμῶνι φλέγμα γεννᾶται κατὰ τὴν κοιλίαν, ἐκκενοῦν αὐτὸ διὰ τῶν ἐμέτων συμβου- λεύει.
τοῦ θέρους δὲ τὴν ἐπιπολάζουσαν ἄνω χολὴν ἀντι- σπᾷν κάτω.
καθαίρειν μέντοι τὸ σύμπαν σῶμα βουληθέν- τι σοι θέρους μὲν διὰ τῆς ἄνω, χειμῶνος δὲ διὰ τῆς κά- τω κοιλίας φαρμακευτέον, ὡς ἐν ἀφορισμοῖς εἴρηται.
τὰ μὲν γὰρ ἤδη πλεονάζοντα ἡ κάθαρσις ἰᾶται διὰ τῶν χω- ρίων ᾗ ῥέπει τὴν κάθαρσιν ποιούμενος.
ἀκτέα γὰρ ᾗ ῥέπει διὰ τῶν συμφερόντων χωρίων.
ὅσα δὲ κωλῦσαι θέλεις αὐξη- θῆναι, διὰ τῶν ἀντικειμένων χωρίων ἀντισπᾷν προσήκει.
Ἔστω δὲ τὰ κατακλύσματα τοῖσιν μὲν παχυτέροισι καὶ ὑγροτέροισιν ἁλμυρώτερα καὶ λεπτότερα, τοῖσι δὲ ξηρο- τέροισι καὶ προσεσταλμένοισι καὶ ἀσθενεστέροισι λιπαρώτερα καὶ παχύτερα.
english_sentences: Just as, then, the bath-keepers say that they 'flush out' (κατακλύζειν) the baths when they wash off the mud and the dirt from the stones in them, so too the flushings (κατακλύσματα) of the stomach and of the [199] intestines wash away the phlegm and the bile from them.
Since, then, in winter phlegm is generated in the belly, he advises evacuating it by means of vomitings; but in summer, drawing the bile that floats up on top back downwards.
If, however, you wish to purge the whole body, you must administer drugs in summer through the upper belly, and in winter through the lower belly, as has been said in the Aphorisms.
For purging cures what is already in excess when one performs the purging through the regions toward which it inclines; for one must lead it where it inclines, through the appropriate regions.
But whatever you wish to prevent from increasing, it is fitting to draw off in the opposite direction through the opposite regions.
Let the flushings be saltier and thinner for those who are stouter and moister, and fattier and thicker for those who are drier, contracted and weaker.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ τῶν κατακλυσμάτων λιπαρὰ καὶ πα- χέα τὰ ἀπὸ τῶν γαλάκτων καὶ ἀπὸ ἐρεβίνθων ὕδωρ ἑφθὲν καὶ [200] τῶν ἄλλων τῶν τοιουτέων, τὰ δὲ λεπτὰ καὶ ἁλμυρὰ ἅλ- μη καὶ θάλασσα καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα.
beads.english: Of the clysters, the fatty and thick ones are those made from milks, and water in which chickpeas have been boiled, and [200] other such things; the thin and salty ones are brine and sea water and the like.

beads.greek: Τὰ τμητικώτερα μὲν ἐπὶ τῶν παχυτέρων ἀξιοῖ προσφέ- ρειν, φλεγματικώτεροι γὰρ οὗτοι· τὰ λειότερα δ᾿ ἐπὶ τῶν ἰσχνῶν, ὡς ἂν χολωδεστέρων ὄντων.
beads.english: He thinks it right to administer the more cutting ones to the stouter, for these are more phlegmatic, and the smoother ones to the lean, since they are more bilious.

beads.greek: ὁποῖαι δέ εἰσιν ἑκατέ- ρων αἱ ὗλαι, διὰ τῆς ἐχομένης ῥήσεως ἐδήλωσεν, ἐξηγή- σεως οὐ δεομένης· διὸ καὶ παραλιπὼν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ τὰ συνεχῆ τρέψομαι.
beads.english: What the materials of each kind are he has made clear in the following passage, which needs no exposition. I shall therefore pass it over and turn to what comes next.

beads.greek: Τοὺς δὲ ἐμέτους ᾧδε χρὴ ποιέεσθαι.
beads.english: Vomitings should be induced as follows.

beads.greek: ὅσοι μὲν τῶν ἀνθρώ- πων παχέες εἰσὶ καὶ μὴ ἰσχνοὶ, νήστιες ἐμούντων, δρα- μόντες ἢ ὁδοιπορήσαντες διὰ τάχεος κατὰ μέσον τῆς ἡμέρης.
beads.english: Those people who are stout and not lean should vomit fasting, after running or walking quickly, at the middle of the day.

greek_sentences: ἔστι δὲ τῶν κατακλυσμάτων λιπαρὰ καὶ πα- χέα τὰ ἀπὸ τῶν γαλάκτων καὶ ἀπὸ ἐρεβίνθων ὕδωρ ἑφθὲν καὶ [200] τῶν ἄλλων τῶν τοιουτέων, τὰ δὲ λεπτὰ καὶ ἁλμυρὰ ἅλ- μη καὶ θάλασσα καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα.
Τὰ τμητικώτερα μὲν ἐπὶ τῶν παχυτέρων ἀξιοῖ προσφέ- ρειν, φλεγματικώτεροι γὰρ οὗτοι· τὰ λειότερα δ᾿ ἐπὶ τῶν ἰσχνῶν, ὡς ἂν χολωδεστέρων ὄντων.
ὁποῖαι δέ εἰσιν ἑκατέ- ρων αἱ ὗλαι, διὰ τῆς ἐχομένης ῥήσεως ἐδήλωσεν, ἐξηγή- σεως οὐ δεομένης· διὸ καὶ παραλιπὼν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ τὰ συνεχῆ τρέψομαι.
Τοὺς δὲ ἐμέτους ᾧδε χρὴ ποιέεσθαι.
ὅσοι μὲν τῶν ἀνθρώ- πων παχέες εἰσὶ καὶ μὴ ἰσχνοὶ, νήστιες ἐμούντων, δρα- μόντες ἢ ὁδοιπορήσαντες διὰ τάχεος κατὰ μέσον τῆς ἡμέρης.
english_sentences: Of the clysters, the fatty and thick ones are those made from milks, and water in which chickpeas have been boiled, and [200] other such things; the thin and salty ones are brine and sea water and the like.
He thinks it right to administer the more cutting ones to the stouter, for these are more phlegmatic, and the smoother ones to the lean, since they are more bilious.
What the materials of each kind are he has made clear in the following passage, which needs no exposition.
I shall therefore pass it over and turn to what comes next.
Vomitings should be induced as follows.
Those people who are stout and not lean should vomit fasting, after running or walking quickly, at the middle of the day.

beads.greek: Ἐκτεθερμάνθαι βούλεται τὸ σῶμα τοῖς παχέσιν, ἐμεῖν μέλλουσιν ἕνεκα τῆς χύσεως τῶν φλεγματικῶν χυμῶν, οὓς [201] πλείους ἔχουσιν οἱ παχεῖς.
beads.english: He wants the body of stout people who are about to vomit to have been thoroughly heated beforehand, for the sake of the liquefaction of the phlegmatic humours, which [201] stout people have in greater quantity.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ τῶν ἀγγείων ἀνα- στόμωσις ἁπάντων τε τῶν κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρων ἀραίωσις οὕτως ἂν μάλιστα γένοιτο.
beads.english: Moreover, the opening of the mouths of the vessels and the rarefaction of all the fine pores would come about best in this way.

beads.greek: χρήσιμα δὲ ταῦτα πάντα πρὸς τὸ ῥᾳδίως τε καὶ ἀλύπως γίνεσθαι τὸν ἔμετον.
beads.english: All these things are useful for making the vomiting take place easily and without distress.

beads.greek: Ἔστω δὲ ἡμικοτύλιον ὑσσώπου τετριμμένου ἐν ὕδα- τος χοέϊ καὶ τοῦτο ἐκπιέτω, ὄξος παραχέων καὶ ἅλας παραβάλλων, ὅκως ἂν μέλλῃ ἥδιστον ἔσεσθαι.
beads.english: Let there be half a kotyle of hyssop, pounded, in a chous of water, and let him drink this off, pouring in vinegar and adding salt, so that it will be as pleasant as possible.

beads.greek: Ὅτι τμητικὸν εἶναι βούλεται τὸ πόμα καὶ δι᾿ ἥντινα αἰτίαν οὐκ ἄδηλον.
beads.english: That he wants the potion to be incisive, and for what reason, is not unclear.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ γὰρ οἱ παχεῖς ἄνθρωποι καὶ τοὺς χυμοὺς ἔχουσι τοὐπίπαν παχεῖς τε καὶ ψυχροὺς καί τινας αὐτῶν καὶ γλίσχρους, διὰ τοῦτο τμητικὸν εἶναι κελεύει τὸ ποτὸν αὐτῶν.
beads.english: For since stout people generally also have humours that are thick and cold, and some of these also viscous, for this reason he bids their drink be incisive.

beads.greek: ὁπόσον δέ τε τὸ πλῆθος δίδωσιν οὗ συντί- θησι πόματα, οὐκ ἀκριβῶς ἔχω φάναι, διὰ τὸ μέτρον ἔστιν ὅτε, ὃ καλοῦσι χοέα, μὴ τὸ αὐτὸ μέγεθος ἔχειν παρὰ πᾶ- σιν.
beads.english: But how great a quantity he gives of the potions he compounds I cannot say exactly, because the measure which they call a chous sometimes does not have the same size among all peoples.

greek_sentences: Ἐκτεθερμάνθαι βούλεται τὸ σῶμα τοῖς παχέσιν, ἐμεῖν μέλλουσιν ἕνεκα τῆς χύσεως τῶν φλεγματικῶν χυμῶν, οὓς [201] πλείους ἔχουσιν οἱ παχεῖς.
ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ τῶν ἀγγείων ἀνα- στόμωσις ἁπάντων τε τῶν κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρων ἀραίωσις οὕτως ἂν μάλιστα γένοιτο.
χρήσιμα δὲ ταῦτα πάντα πρὸς τὸ ῥᾳδίως τε καὶ ἀλύπως γίνεσθαι τὸν ἔμετον.
Ἔστω δὲ ἡμικοτύλιον ὑσσώπου τετριμμένου ἐν ὕδα- τος χοέϊ καὶ τοῦτο ἐκπιέτω, ὄξος παραχέων καὶ ἅλας παραβάλλων, ὅκως ἂν μέλλῃ ἥδιστον ἔσεσθαι.
Ὅτι τμητικὸν εἶναι βούλεται τὸ πόμα καὶ δι᾿ ἥντινα αἰτίαν οὐκ ἄδηλον.
ἐπεὶ γὰρ οἱ παχεῖς ἄνθρωποι καὶ τοὺς χυμοὺς ἔχουσι τοὐπίπαν παχεῖς τε καὶ ψυχροὺς καί τινας αὐτῶν καὶ γλίσχρους, διὰ τοῦτο τμητικὸν εἶναι κελεύει τὸ ποτὸν αὐτῶν.
ὁπόσον δέ τε τὸ πλῆθος δίδωσιν οὗ συντί- θησι πόματα, οὐκ ἀκριβῶς ἔχω φάναι, διὰ τὸ μέτρον ἔστιν ὅτε, ὃ καλοῦσι χοέα, μὴ τὸ αὐτὸ μέγεθος ἔχειν παρὰ πᾶ- σιν.
english_sentences: He wants the body of stout people who are about to vomit to have been thoroughly heated beforehand, for the sake of the liquefaction of the phlegmatic humours, which [201] stout people have in greater quantity.
Moreover, the opening of the mouths of the vessels and the rarefaction of all the fine pores would come about best in this way.
All these things are useful for making the vomiting take place easily and without distress.
Let there be half a kotyle of hyssop, pounded, in a chous of water, and let him drink this off, pouring in vinegar and adding salt, so that it will be as pleasant as possible.
That he wants the potion to be incisive, and for what reason, is not unclear.
For since stout people generally also have humours that are thick and cold, and some of these also viscous, for this reason he bids their drink be incisive.
But how great a quantity he gives of the potions he compounds I cannot say exactly, because the measure which they call a chous sometimes does not have the same size among all peoples.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ τὸν Ἀττικὸν κελεύει πίνειν, οὐ πάνυ συντίθεμαι [202] τῷ ἔθει, πολὺ γὰρ εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ.
beads.english: But if he orders him to drink the Attic [chous], I do not entirely agree [202] with the custom, for it seems to me to be a large amount.

beads.greek: σύνηθες μέντοι τοῖς παλαιοῖς ἦν, εἴτε ὀῤῥῷ γάλακτος εἴτε τοιούτῳ τινὶ κατα- κλύσματι προείλοντο χρῆσθαι, πάμπολυ τῷ πλήθει διδόναι.
beads.english: It was, however, customary among the ancients, whether they chose to use whey of milk or some other such flushing draught, to give a very great quantity.

beads.greek: Πινέτω δὲ τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ἡσυχέστερον, ἔπειτα δὲ ἐπὶ θᾶσσον.
beads.english: Let him drink at first more gently, and thereafter more quickly.

beads.greek: Ἐὰν μὲν οὖν ἐν ἀρχῇ πίῃ λάβρως, εὐθέως ἐμεῖται, πρὶν ἐκπίῃ τὸ πᾶν, ἀποῤῥύψαι τε τοὺς ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ χυ- μοὺς, οἷς συνεκκενοῦνται καὶ οἱ κατὰ τὰς πρώτας φλέβας.
beads.english: If, then, at the beginning he drinks greedily, he will vomit at once, before he has drunk the whole and before it can wash off the humours in the stomach, together with which those in the first veins are also evacuated.

beads.greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν ἡσυχέστερον, ὕστερον δὲ πλεῖον πάντως πίῃ, οὕτω δυνήσεται χρόνῳ τε συμμέτρῳ κατασχεῖν, ὁρμή- σει τε πρὸς ἔμετον ἐν καιρῷ διὰ τὸ πίνειν ἀθροώτερον ὕστερον.
beads.english: But if at the beginning he drinks more gently, and later drinks altogether more, he will thus be able to retain it for a proportionate time, and he will be impelled towards vomiting at the right moment, because he later drinks more all at once.

greek_sentences: εἰ δὲ τὸν Ἀττικὸν κελεύει πίνειν, οὐ πάνυ συντίθεμαι [202] τῷ ἔθει, πολὺ γὰρ εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ.

If, then, at the beginning he drinks greedily, he will vomit at once, before he has drunk the whole and before it can wash off the humours in the stomach, together with which those in the first veins are also evacuated.

But if at the beginning he drinks more gently, and later drinks altogether more, he will thus be able to retain it for a proportionate time, and he will be impelled towards vomiting at the right moment, because he later drinks more all at once.

beads.greek: Οἱ δὲ λεπτότεροι καὶ ἀσθενέστεροι ἀπὸ σιτίων ποιεέσθω- [203] σαν τὸν ἔμετον τρόπῳ τοιῷδε.
beads.english: Those who are thinner and weaker should induce vomiting after food in the following manner.

beads.greek: λουσάμενοι θερμῷ προ- πιέτωσαν ἀκρήτου κοτύλην, ἔπειτα σιτία παντοδαπὰ ἐσθι- έτωσαν καὶ μὴ πινέτωσαν ἐπὶ τῷ σιτίῳ, μηδὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ σιτίου, ἀλλὰ ἐπισχέτωσαν ὅσον τέσσαρα στάδια διελθεῖν.
beads.english: Having bathed in hot water, let them first drink a kotyle of unmixed wine; then let them eat foods of every kind, and let them not drink with the food nor after the food, but let them wait as long as it takes to walk four stades.

beads.greek: ἔπειτα δὲ συμμίξας οἴνους τρεῖς πίνειν διδόναι αὐστηρὸν καὶ γλυκὺν καὶ ὀξύν.
beads.english: Then, having mixed three wines, give them to drink: a dry one, a sweet one and a sharp one.

beads.greek: πρῶτον μὲν ἀκρητέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ χρόνου. ἔπειτα δὲ ὑδαρέστερόν τε καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλόν.
beads.english: First less diluted, a little at a time and at long intervals; then more watered, faster, and in large quantity.

beads.greek: Λουσάμενον θερμῷ προπίνειν ἀξιοῖ πόματος ἀκρατεστέ- ρῳ, λογισμῷ τοιῷδε χρώμενος, ὡς ἂν εἰκάσειέ τις.
beads.english: He wants the person who has bathed in hot water to drink beforehand a less diluted drink, using some such reasoning as one might conjecture.

beads.greek: ἐκ τοῦ θερμοῦ λουτροῦ θερμαίνεται πᾶν τὸ σῶμα καὶ οἱ χυ- μοὶ χέονται καὶ χαλαρὰ γίνονται τὰ ἀγγεῖα, τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ ὁ ἀκρατέστερος οἶνος ἐργάζεται, μετὰ τοῦ καὶ ῥωννύναι τὴν δύναμιν, ἧς μάλιστα φροντίζειν ἔοικεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἰσχνῶν.
beads.english: From the hot bath the whole [203] body is warmed, the humours are made to flow, and the vessels become slack; and the less diluted wine produces these very same effects, while also strengthening the strength, for which he seems to be most concerned in the case of the lean.

beads.greek: ἔπειτα, φησὶ, σιτία παντοδαπὰ ἐσθι- έτωσαν. τούτου δὲ λογισμὸν οὐ τὸν αὐτὸν πάντες ἔγραψαν οἱ ἐξηγησάμενοι τὸ βιβλίον.
beads.english: 'Then,' he says, 'let them eat foods of every kind.' Not all those who have expounded the book have written the same reasoning for this.

greek_sentences: Οἱ δὲ λεπτότεροι καὶ ἀσθενέστεροι ἀπὸ σιτίων ποιεέσθω- [203] σαν τὸν ἔμετον τρόπῳ τοιῷδε.

ἔπειτα δὲ συμμίξας οἴνους τρεῖς πίνειν διδόναι αὐστηρὸν καὶ γλυκὺν καὶ ὀξύν.
πρῶτον μὲν ἀκρητέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ χρόνου.
ἔπειτα δὲ ὑδαρέστερόν τε καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλόν.
Λουσάμενον θερμῷ προπίνειν ἀξιοῖ πόματος ἀκρατεστέ- ρῳ, λογισμῷ τοιῷδε χρώμενος, ὡς ἂν εἰκάσειέ τις.

ἐκ τοῦ θερμοῦ λουτροῦ θερμαίνεται πᾶν τὸ σῶμα καὶ οἱ χυ- μοὶ χέονται καὶ χαλαρὰ γίνονται τὰ ἀγγεῖα, τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ ὁ ἀκρατέστερος οἶνος ἐργάζεται, μετὰ τοῦ καὶ ῥωννύναι τὴν δύναμιν, ἧς μάλιστα φροντίζειν ἔοικεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἰσχνῶν.
ἔπειτα, φησὶ, σιτία παντοδαπὰ ἐσθι- έτωσαν.
τούτου δὲ λογισμὸν οὐ τὸν αὐτὸν πάντες ἔγραψαν οἱ ἐξηγησάμενοι τὸ βιβλίον.
english_sentences: Those who are thinner and weaker should induce vomiting after food in the following manner.

Having bathed in hot water, let them first drink a kotyle of unmixed wine; then let them eat foods of every kind, and let them not drink with the food nor after the food, but let them wait as long as it takes to walk four stades.
Then, having mixed three wines, give them to drink: a dry one, a sweet one and a sharp one.
First less diluted, a little at a time and at long intervals; then more watered, faster, and in large quantity.
He wants the person who has bathed in hot water to drink beforehand a less diluted drink, using some such reasoning as one might conjecture.

From the hot bath the whole [203] body is warmed, the humours are made to flow, and the vessels become slack; and the less diluted wine produces these very same effects, while also strengthening the strength, for which he seems to be most concerned in the case of the lean.
'Then,' he says, 'let them eat foods of every kind.' Not all those who have expounded the book have written the same reasoning for this.

beads.greek: ἐνίοις μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν δοκεῖ διδόναι παντοδαπὰ, διότι στασιάζοντα πρὸς ἄλληλα ῥᾷον εἰς ﻿ [204] ἔμετον ὁρμᾷ, τισὶ δὲ ὑπὲρ τοῦ πλεῖον προσενεγκέσθαι.
beads.english: For to some of them he seems to give all sorts of foods because, being at variance with one another, they more readily impel toward [204] vomiting; to others, in order that more be taken in.

beads.greek: τὰ γὰρ ἁπλᾶ καὶ μονοειδῆ ταχέως ἐμπίπλησιν, οὐκ ἐᾷ δὲ πί- νειν εὐθέως αὐτοὺς, ἵνα μὴ ταχέως ἐπιπολάσῃ τὰ σιτία, ὅ οὐ βούλεται.
beads.english: For simple and uniform foods quickly fill one up. He does not allow them to drink at once, so that the foods do not quickly rise to the surface, which he does not want.

beads.greek: διὰ δὲ τὸ μὴ γενέσθαι τοῦτο καὶ χρόνον τινὰ μεταξὺ πρὸς τὴν θρέψιν αὐτάρκη διατρίβειν ὁρίζει καὶ τὸν χρόνον δὲ αὐτὸν εἶπεν, ὅσον τεσσάρων σταδίων διελθεῖν.
beads.english: And so that this does not happen, he also prescribes spending some interval of time in between, sufficient for nutrition, and he stated the time itself: as long as it takes to walk four stades.

beads.greek: ἐπὶ δὲ τούτοις, οὕτω προαχθεῖσι, δίδωσι τὸ ποτὸν, οἴνους τρεῖς διαφέροντας ἀλλήλων κατὰ ποιότητα.
beads.english: Then, to those thus prepared, he gives the drink: three wines differing from one another in quality.

beads.greek: κελεύει γὰρ εἶ- ναι τὸν μέν τινα τῶν οἴνων αὐστηρὸν, τὸν δὲ γλυκὺν, τὸν δὲ ὀξύν. οὐκ εἰπὼν οὐδὲ ἐνταῦθα τὴν αἰτίαν, δι᾿ ἣν οὕτως ἐκέλευσεν.
beads.english: For he orders that one of the wines be austere, another sweet, and another sour, without stating here either the cause for which he gave this order.

beads.greek: οἱ δ᾿ ἀπομαντευόμενοι τῆς γνώμης αὐτοῦ φασὶ τὸν μὲν αὐστηρὸν διδόναι ῥώμης ἕνεκα τῶν ὀργάνων, δι᾿ ὦν ὁ ἔμετος ἔσται, τὸν δὲ γλυκὺν ἵνα εἰς ἔμετον ὁρμήσῃ καὶ διὰ τὸ χέειν τοὺς χυμοὺς τὸν γλυκὺν οἶνον, τὸν δ᾿ ὀξὺν ἵνα ἀποῤῥύψῃ τὰ ἐμπεπλασμένα τῇ γαστρί.
beads.english: Those who divine his intention say that he gives the austere wine for the sake of strengthening the organs through which the vomiting will take place; the sweet so that it may impel toward vomiting, and because sweet wine liquefies the humours; and the sour so that it may cleanse away what is plastered onto the stomach.

beads.greek: τάχα γοῦν καὶ τὰ σιτία παντοδαπὰ κατὰ τὰς ποιότητας ἐκέλευσε λαμβά- νειν αὐτοὺς, ἵνα τὰ μὲν ῥώσῃ τὴν γαστέρα, τὰ δὲ εἰς ἔμε- τον παροξύνῃ, τὰ δὲ ἀποῤῥύψῃ τοὺς ἐμπεπλασμένους χυμούς.
beads.english: Perhaps, then, he also ordered them to take foods of all kinds in respect of their qualities, so that some might strengthen the stomach, others provoke to vomiting, and others cleanse away the humours plastered on.

διὰ δὲ τὸ μὴ γενέσθαι τοῦτο καὶ χρόνον τινὰ μεταξὺ πρὸς τὴν θρέψιν αὐτάρκη διατρίβειν ὁρίζει καὶ τὸν χρόνον δὲ αὐτὸν εἶπεν, ὅσον τεσσάρων σταδίων διελθεῖν.
ἐπὶ δὲ τούτοις, οὕτω προαχθεῖσι, δίδωσι τὸ ποτὸν, οἴνους τρεῖς διαφέροντας ἀλλήλων κατὰ ποιότητα.
κελεύει γὰρ εἶ- ναι τὸν μέν τινα τῶν οἴνων αὐστηρὸν, τὸν δὲ γλυκὺν, τὸν δὲ ὀξύν.
οὐκ εἰπὼν οὐδὲ ἐνταῦθα τὴν αἰτίαν, δι᾿ ἣν οὕτως ἐκέλευσεν.

οἱ δ᾿ ἀπομαντευόμενοι τῆς γνώμης αὐτοῦ φασὶ τὸν μὲν αὐστηρὸν διδόναι ῥώμης ἕνεκα τῶν ὀργάνων, δι᾿ ὦν ὁ ἔμετος ἔσται, τὸν δὲ γλυκὺν ἵνα εἰς ἔμετον ὁρμήσῃ καὶ διὰ τὸ χέειν τοὺς χυμοὺς τὸν γλυκὺν οἶνον, τὸν δ᾿ ὀξὺν ἵνα ἀποῤῥύψῃ τὰ ἐμπεπλασμένα τῇ γαστρί.

english_sentences: For to some of them he seems to give all sorts of foods because, being at variance with one another, they more readily impel toward [204] vomiting; to others, in order that more be taken in.
For simple and uniform foods quickly fill one up.
He does not allow them to drink at once, so that the foods do not quickly rise to the surface, which he does not want.
And so that this does not happen, he also prescribes spending some interval of time in between, sufficient for nutrition, and he stated the time itself: as long as it takes to walk four stades.
Then, to those thus prepared, he gives the drink: three wines differing from one another in quality.
For he orders that one of the wines be austere, another sweet, and another sour, without stating here either the cause for which he gave this order.

Those who divine his intention say that he gives the austere wine for the sake of strengthening the organs through which the vomiting will take place; the sweet so that it may impel toward vomiting, and because sweet wine liquefies the humours; and the sour so that it may cleanse away what is plastered onto the stomach.

Perhaps, then, he also ordered them to take foods of all kinds in respect of their qualities, so that some might strengthen the stomach, others provoke to vomiting, and others cleanse away the humours plastered on.

beads.greek: [205] ὅπερ δὲ λέγω πολλάκις ἐν ταῖς πρὸς τοὺς ἑταίρους τε καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους φίλους συνουσίαις, ἐρῶ καὶ νῦν.
beads.english: [205] What I often say in my conversations with my companions and with my other friends, I shall say now as well.

beads.greek: οὐ σμικρά μοι δοκοῦσιν ἁμαρτάνειν οἱ τὴν δογματικὴν αἵρεσιν ἄνδρες πρεσβεύοντες, ἄνευ τοῦ τὸν λογισμὸν εἰπεῖν ὦν συμβουλεύ- ουσιν, ἀποφαινόμενοι καθάπερ τινὰ προστάγματα βασιλικά.
beads.english: Those men who champion the Dogmatic sect seem to me to err in no small way when, without stating the reasoning behind what they advise, they make pronouncements like royal decrees.

beads.greek: βέλτιον γὰρ ἦν ἑκάστου τῶν πραττομένων αὐτὸν τὸν γρά- ψαντα τὸ βιβλίον εἰπεῖν τὴν δύναμιν, ὡς Ἱπποκράτης ἐποί- ησεν ἐν τῷ περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων, ἐπὶ τῆς πτισάνης εἰπών. τὸ γὰρ γλίσχρον αὐτῆς λεῖον καὶ προσηνὲς καὶ συνεχές ἐστι καὶ ὀλισθηρὸν καὶ πλαδαρὸν μετρίως καὶ ἄδιψον καὶ εὐέκ- πλυτον, εἴ τι καὶ τούτου προσδέοι καὶ οὔτε στύψιν ἔχον, οὔτε ἄραδον κακὸν, οὔτε ἀνοιδίσκεται ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.
beads.english: For it would have been better for the author of the book himself to state the power of each of the things that are done, as Hippocrates did in On Regimen in Acute Diseases when he said of ptisane: 'For its viscid substance is smooth, soothing, continuous, slippery, moderately moist, free from thirst, and easily washed out, if there should be any need of this too; it has neither astringency nor bad disturbance, nor does it swell up in the belly.' In the same way he also wrote about melicrat, wine and oxymel, and further about baths, so that we have a starting point for the method by which we may add, in agreement with the writer, some of the things not said by him.

beads.greek: οὕτως δὲ καὶ περὶ μελικράτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὀξυμέλιτος, ἔτι τε λουτρῶν ἔγραψεν, ὥστε ἀρχὴν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς τῆς ὁδοῦ καθ᾿ ἣν ἀκολούθως τῷ συγγραφεῖ τῶν οὐκ εἰρημένων ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ προς- θῶμέν τινα. καὶ νῦν οὖν εἰρηκότος αὐτοῦ τἄλλα, χωρὶς τοῦ τῆς αἰτίας λογισμοῦ καὶ μέντοι ὡς ἤτοι πίνειν ἔνεστι τὸν οἶνον πρῶτον μὲν ἀκρητέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ, ἔπειτα δὲ ὑδαρέστερόν τε καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλόν.
beads.english: And now, then, since he has stated the rest without the reasoning of the cause, and moreover that one may drink the wine first rather undiluted, a little at a time and at long intervals, and then more watered, more quickly and in large quantity,

greek_sentences: [205] ὅπερ δὲ λέγω πολλάκις ἐν ταῖς πρὸς τοὺς ἑταίρους τε καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους φίλους συνουσίαις, ἐρῶ καὶ νῦν.
οὐ σμικρά μοι δοκοῦσιν ἁμαρτάνειν οἱ τὴν δογματικὴν αἵρεσιν ἄνδρες πρεσβεύοντες, ἄνευ τοῦ τὸν λογισμὸν εἰπεῖν ὦν συμβουλεύ- ουσιν, ἀποφαινόμενοι καθάπερ τινὰ προστάγματα βασιλικά.
βέλτιον γὰρ ἦν ἑκάστου τῶν πραττομένων αὐτὸν τὸν γρά- ψαντα τὸ βιβλίον εἰπεῖν τὴν δύναμιν, ὡς Ἱπποκράτης ἐποί- ησεν ἐν τῷ περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων, ἐπὶ τῆς πτισάνης εἰπών.

τὸ γὰρ γλίσχρον αὐτῆς λεῖον καὶ προσηνὲς καὶ συνεχές ἐστι καὶ ὀλισθηρὸν καὶ πλαδαρὸν μετρίως καὶ ἄδιψον καὶ εὐέκ- πλυτον, εἴ τι καὶ τούτου προσδέοι καὶ οὔτε στύψιν ἔχον, οὔτε ἄραδον κακὸν, οὔτε ἀνοιδίσκεται ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.
οὕτως δὲ καὶ περὶ μελικράτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὀξυμέλιτος, ἔτι τε λουτρῶν ἔγραψεν, ὥστε ἀρχὴν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς τῆς ὁδοῦ καθ᾿ ἣν ἀκολούθως τῷ συγγραφεῖ τῶν οὐκ εἰρημένων ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ προς- θῶμέν τινα.

καὶ νῦν οὖν εἰρηκότος αὐτοῦ τἄλλα, χωρὶς τοῦ τῆς αἰτίας λογισμοῦ καὶ μέντοι ὡς ἤτοι πίνειν ἔνεστι τὸν οἶνον πρῶτον μὲν ἀκρητέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ, ἔπειτα δὲ ὑδαρέστερόν τε καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλόν.
english_sentences: [205] What I often say in my conversations with my companions and with my other friends, I shall say now as well.
Those men who champion the Dogmatic sect seem to me to err in no small way when, without stating the reasoning behind what they advise, they make pronouncements like royal decrees.

For it would have been better for the author of the book himself to state the power of each of the things that are done, as Hippocrates did in On Regimen in Acute Diseases when he said of ptisane: 'For its viscid substance is smooth, soothing, continuous, slippery, moderately moist, free from thirst, and easily washed out, if there should be any need of this too; it has neither astringency nor bad disturbance, nor does it swell up in the belly.' In the same way he also wrote about melicrat, wine and oxymel, and further about baths, so that we have a starting point for the method by which we may add, in agreement with the writer, some of the things not said by him.

And now, then, since he has stated the rest without the reasoning of the cause, and moreover that one may drink the wine first rather undiluted, a little at a time and at long intervals, and then more watered, more quickly and in large quantity,

beads.greek: ἡμᾶς [206] δεῖ στοχάζεσθαι τῆς γνώμης αὐτοῦ, καθ᾿ ἣν ἔγραψεν.
beads.english: we [206] must conjecture his intention, in accordance with which he wrote.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἄλλως μὲν ἅπας στοχασμὸς ἀμφίβολον πρᾶγμα· μάλιστα δὲ ὅταν ἔτ᾿ ἀνθρώπου γνώμη ἠγνόηται.
beads.english: Every conjecture is in any case an ambiguous matter, but most of all when the man's intention is still unknown.

beads.greek: τὸ μὲν οὖν ὑδαρέστε- ρον πίνειν τὸν οἶνον καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλὸν εἰκότως ἂν εἰρῆσθαι δόξειεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐμεῖν ἐθελόντων, εἴπερ γε καὶ τἀν- αντία τοῖς κατασχεῖν βουλομένοις καὶ πέψαι τὴν τροφὴν ἐστὶν ἐπιτήδεια, τό τε ἀκρατέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ.
beads.english: Now, drinking the wine more watery, more quickly and in large quantity might reasonably seem to have been said with reference to those who wish to vomit, since the opposite things are suitable for those who want to retain and digest their food: wine less diluted, in small quantity and at long intervals.

beads.greek: διὰ τί δ᾿ ὅλως τὰ πρὸς τὸ κατασχεῖν ἁρμόττοντα πρῶτα παρ- έλαβεν ἐπὶ τοῦ μέλλοντος ἐμεῖν ὀλίγον ὕστερον, οὐκ ἔχομεν εἰ- πεῖν τι πιθανόν.
beads.english: But why he took up first at all the things suited to retaining the food, in the case of someone who is going to vomit a little later, we cannot say anything plausible.

beads.greek: ἴσως δ᾿ ἐκείνῳ τῷ γράψαντι ταῦτα πιθα- νὸν ἐδόκει τὸ καὶ τῶν ἐξηγητῶν ἐνίοις ἀρέσκον. ἐπειδὴ βού- λεται μὴ καταλύεσθαι τὴν δύναμιν τῶν λεπτῶν ἀνθρώπων ὑπὲρ ὦν ταῦτα γράφει, διὰ τοῦτ᾿ οὖν πρώτην ἐκείνην ῥώννυ- σιν, εἶθ᾿ οὕτως ἐπὶ τὰ τὸν ἔμετον κινοῦντα παραγίνεται.
beads.english: Perhaps the man who wrote this found plausible the view that also pleases some of the commentators: since he wishes the strength of the thin people for whom he writes this not to be broken down, for this reason he first strengthens it, and only then proceeds to what provokes vomiting.

beads.greek: ἀλλ᾿ εἰς τὸ ῥωσθῆναι τὴν δύναμιν αὐτάρκης ἦν ὁ ἐπὶ τῇ τῶν σι- τίων προσφορᾷ χρόνος.
beads.english: But for the strength to be fortified, the time spent on the taking of the foods was sufficient.

beads.greek: ἄλλο δὲ ἄλλῳ πιθανὸν, ὡς ἔφην, ἐστὶν, οὐκ ἀποτετμημένον, ὡς ἕν τι, καθάπερ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον, ὃ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιστημονικὰς ἀποδείξεις βεβαιοῦται.
beads.english: As I said, one thing is plausible to one man and another to another. It is not marked off as a single determinate thing, as the necessary is, which is confirmed by scientific demonstrations.

greek_sentences: ἡμᾶς [206] δεῖ στοχάζεσθαι τῆς γνώμης αὐτοῦ, καθ᾿ ἣν ἔγραψεν.
ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἄλλως μὲν ἅπας στοχασμὸς ἀμφίβολον πρᾶγμα· μάλιστα δὲ ὅταν ἔτ᾿ ἀνθρώπου γνώμη ἠγνόηται.

τὸ μὲν οὖν ὑδαρέστε- ρον πίνειν τὸν οἶνον καὶ θᾶσσον καὶ κατὰ πολλὸν εἰκότως ἂν εἰρῆσθαι δόξειεν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐμεῖν ἐθελόντων, εἴπερ γε καὶ τἀν- αντία τοῖς κατασχεῖν βουλομένοις καὶ πέψαι τὴν τροφὴν ἐστὶν ἐπιτήδεια, τό τε ἀκρατέστερον καὶ κατ᾿ ὀλίγον καὶ διὰ πολλοῦ.
διὰ τί δ᾿ ὅλως τὰ πρὸς τὸ κατασχεῖν ἁρμόττοντα πρῶτα παρ- έλαβεν ἐπὶ τοῦ μέλλοντος ἐμεῖν ὀλίγον ὕστερον, οὐκ ἔχομεν εἰ- πεῖν τι πιθανόν.
ἴσως δ᾿ ἐκείνῳ τῷ γράψαντι ταῦτα πιθα- νὸν ἐδόκει τὸ καὶ τῶν ἐξηγητῶν ἐνίοις ἀρέσκον.
ἐπειδὴ βού- λεται μὴ καταλύεσθαι τὴν δύναμιν τῶν λεπτῶν ἀνθρώπων ὑπὲρ ὦν ταῦτα γράφει, διὰ τοῦτ᾿ οὖν πρώτην ἐκείνην ῥώννυ- σιν, εἶθ᾿ οὕτως ἐπὶ τὰ τὸν ἔμετον κινοῦντα παραγίνεται.
ἀλλ᾿ εἰς τὸ ῥωσθῆναι τὴν δύναμιν αὐτάρκης ἦν ὁ ἐπὶ τῇ τῶν σι- τίων προσφορᾷ χρόνος.
ἄλλο δὲ ἄλλῳ πιθανὸν, ὡς ἔφην, ἐστὶν, οὐκ ἀποτετμημένον, ὡς ἕν τι, καθάπερ τὸ ἀναγκαῖον, ὃ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιστημονικὰς ἀποδείξεις βεβαιοῦται.
english_sentences: we [206] must conjecture his intention, in accordance with which he wrote.
Every conjecture is in any case an ambiguous matter, but most of all when the man's intention is still unknown.

Now, drinking the wine more watery, more quickly and in large quantity might reasonably seem to have been said with reference to those who wish to vomit, since the opposite things are suitable for those who want to retain and digest their food: wine less diluted, in small quantity and at long intervals.
But why he took up first at all the things suited to retaining the food, in the case of someone who is going to vomit a little later, we cannot say anything plausible.

Perhaps the man who wrote this found plausible the view that also pleases some of the commentators: since he wishes the strength of the thin people for whom he writes this not to be broken down, for this reason he first strengthens it, and only then proceeds to what provokes vomiting.
But for the strength to be fortified, the time spent on the taking of the foods was sufficient.
As I said, one thing is plausible to one man and another to another.
It is not marked off as a single determinate thing, as the necessary is, which is confirmed by scientific demonstrations.

beads.greek: [207] Ὅστις δὲ εἴωθε τοῦ μηνὸς δὶς ἐξεμέειν, ἄμεινον ἐφε- ξῆς ποιέεσθαι τοὺς ἐμέτους ἐν δυσὶν ἡμέρῃσι μᾶλλον ἢ διὰ πεντεκαίδεκα.
beads.english: [207] Whoever is accustomed to vomit twice a month, it is better for him to do the vomiting on two successive days rather than at intervals of fifteen days.

beads.greek: οἱ δὲ πᾶν τοὐναντίον ποιέουσι.
beads.english: But people do the very opposite.

beads.greek: Καὶ τούτων τὸν λογισμὸν αὐτὸν ἔδει τὸν γράψαντα προστεθεικέναι μάλιστα, ἐπειδὴ καὶ χωρὶς διορισμοῦ περὶ τῶν δὶς ἐμούντων εἶπεν ἐν τῷ μηνί.
beads.english: The writer himself ought above all to have added the reasoning for these things as well, since he spoke about those who vomit twice in the month without any distinction.

beads.greek: τινὰς μὲν γὰρ ὁρῶ κενώσεως ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦντας, ὥσπερ καὶ νηστεύοντας ἄλλους ἐν τῷ μηνὶ μίαν ἡμέραν.
beads.english: For I see some people vomiting for the sake of evacuation, just as others fast for one day in the month; and some in order to clean out the humour, whether viscid or thick, that has settled in the stomach.

beads.greek: ἐνίους δὲ τοῦ τὸν ἐνιζηκότα τῇ γα- στρὶ χυμὸν ἢ γλίσχρον ἢ παχὺν ἐκκαθᾶραι, κωλύει δ᾿ οὐ- δὲν ἀμφότερα ἐκ διαλείμματος αὐτὰ ποιεῖν, οὐκ ἐφεξῆς ἡμέ- ραις δύο.
beads.english: Yet nothing prevents doing both of these at an interval, and not on two successive days.

greek_sentences: [207] Ὅστις δὲ εἴωθε τοῦ μηνὸς δὶς ἐξεμέειν, ἄμεινον ἐφε- ξῆς ποιέεσθαι τοὺς ἐμέτους ἐν δυσὶν ἡμέρῃσι μᾶλλον ἢ διὰ πεντεκαίδεκα.
οἱ δὲ πᾶν τοὐναντίον ποιέουσι.
Καὶ τούτων τὸν λογισμὸν αὐτὸν ἔδει τὸν γράψαντα προστεθεικέναι μάλιστα, ἐπειδὴ καὶ χωρὶς διορισμοῦ περὶ τῶν δὶς ἐμούντων εἶπεν ἐν τῷ μηνί.
τινὰς μὲν γὰρ ὁρῶ κενώσεως ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦντας, ὥσπερ καὶ νηστεύοντας ἄλλους ἐν τῷ μηνὶ μίαν ἡμέραν.
ἐνίους δὲ τοῦ τὸν ἐνιζηκότα τῇ γα- στρὶ χυμὸν ἢ γλίσχρον ἢ παχὺν ἐκκαθᾶραι, κωλύει δ᾿ οὐ- δὲν ἀμφότερα ἐκ διαλείμματος αὐτὰ ποιεῖν, οὐκ ἐφεξῆς ἡμέ- ραις δύο.
english_sentences: [207] Whoever is accustomed to vomit twice a month, it is better for him to do the vomiting on two successive days rather than at intervals of fifteen days.
But people do the very opposite.
The writer himself ought above all to have added the reasoning for these things as well, since he spoke about those who vomit twice in the month without any distinction.

For I see some people vomiting for the sake of evacuation, just as others fast for one day in the month; and some in order to clean out the humour, whether viscid or thick, that has settled in the stomach.
Yet nothing prevents doing both of these at an interval, and not on two successive days.

beads.greek: Ὁκόσοισι μὲν ἀνεπιτήδειον ἀπεμέειν τὰ σιτία, ἢ ὁκόσοισιν αἱ κοιλίαι οὐκ εὐδιέξοδοί εἰσι, τουτέοισι πᾶσι ξυμφέρει πολλάκις τῆς ἡμέρης ἐσθίειν καὶ παντοδαποῖσι βρώμασι [208] χρέεσθαι καὶ ὄψοισι πάντας τρόπους ἐσκευασμένοισι καὶ οἴνους τε πίνειν δισσοὺς ἢ τρισσούς.
beads.english: Those for whom it is suitable to vomit up their food, or whose bellies are not easy of passage: for all these it is beneficial to eat many times a day, to make use of all kinds of foods [208] and of relishes prepared in every manner, and to drink two or three wines.

beads.greek: ὁκόσοισι δὲ μὴ ἀνεμέουσι τὰ σιτία, ἢ καὶ κοιλίας ἔχουσιν ὑγρὰς, τουτέοισι πᾶσιν ἐναντίον τουτέου τοῦ τρόπου ξυμφέρει ποιέειν.
beads.english: But those who do not vomit up their food, or who also have moist bellies: for all these it is beneficial to do the opposite of this manner.

beads.greek: Ἐπιτήδειον μὲν ἀνεμεῖν τὰ σιτία τοῖς ἤτοι διαῤῥύψαι βουλομένοις τὴν κοιλίαν, ἢ κένωσιν μετρίαν ποιήσασθαι τοῦ παντός.
beads.english: It is suitable to vomit up food for those who wish either to cleanse out the belly or to make a moderate evacuation of the whole.

beads.greek: ἀξιοῖ δὲ τούτους ἐσθίειν τε πολλάκις καὶ ποικίλα καὶ οἴνους πλείονας πίνειν.
beads.english: He thinks it right that these should eat often and eat varied things, and drink several wines.

beads.greek: ἔμπαλιν δὲ τοὺς μήτε ἐμεῖν βουλομένους, ὑγροτέρας τε τοῦ προσήκοντος ἔχοντας κοιλίας, ὡς ἐπισχέσεως δεῖσθαι, μήτε πο- λλάκις ἐσθίειν, μήτε πολυειδῆ σιτία τε καὶ οἴνους προσφέρεσθαι.
beads.english: Conversely, those who do not wish to vomit and who have bellies moister than is proper, so as to require checking, should neither eat often nor take foods and wines of many kinds.

beads.greek: τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἅπαξ φαγεῖν ἕν τι μονοειδὲς ἔνα τε πίνειν οἶνον εἰς τὸ κατα- σχεῖν αὐτὰ τὴν γαστέρα τε καὶ πέψαι συντελεῖ, τὰ δὲ ἐναντία πεφθῆναί τε δυσχερέστερα καὶ μεῖναι κατὰ τὴν γα- στέρα.
beads.english: For eating once some single uniform thing and drinking one wine contributes to the stomach's retaining them and concocting them, whereas the opposite things are both harder to concoct and harder to remain in the stomach.

greek_sentences: Ὁκόσοισι μὲν ἀνεπιτήδειον ἀπεμέειν τὰ σιτία, ἢ ὁκόσοισιν αἱ κοιλίαι οὐκ εὐδιέξοδοί εἰσι, τουτέοισι πᾶσι ξυμφέρει πολλάκις τῆς ἡμέρης ἐσθίειν καὶ παντοδαποῖσι βρώμασι [208] χρέεσθαι καὶ ὄψοισι πάντας τρόπους ἐσκευασμένοισι καὶ οἴνους τε πίνειν δισσοὺς ἢ τρισσούς.
ὁκόσοισι δὲ μὴ ἀνεμέουσι τὰ σιτία, ἢ καὶ κοιλίας ἔχουσιν ὑγρὰς, τουτέοισι πᾶσιν ἐναντίον τουτέου τοῦ τρόπου ξυμφέρει ποιέειν.
Ἐπιτήδειον μὲν ἀνεμεῖν τὰ σιτία τοῖς ἤτοι διαῤῥύψαι βουλομένοις τὴν κοιλίαν, ἢ κένωσιν μετρίαν ποιήσασθαι τοῦ παντός.
ἀξιοῖ δὲ τούτους ἐσθίειν τε πολλάκις καὶ ποικίλα καὶ οἴνους πλείονας πίνειν.
ἔμπαλιν δὲ τοὺς μήτε ἐμεῖν βουλομένους, ὑγροτέρας τε τοῦ προσήκοντος ἔχοντας κοιλίας, ὡς ἐπισχέσεως δεῖσθαι, μήτε πο- λλάκις ἐσθίειν, μήτε πολυειδῆ σιτία τε καὶ οἴνους προσφέρεσθαι.
τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἅπαξ φαγεῖν ἕν τι μονοειδὲς ἔνα τε πίνειν οἶνον εἰς τὸ κατα- σχεῖν αὐτὰ τὴν γαστέρα τε καὶ πέψαι συντελεῖ, τὰ δὲ ἐναντία πεφθῆναί τε δυσχερέστερα καὶ μεῖναι κατὰ τὴν γα- στέρα.
english_sentences: Those for whom it is suitable to vomit up their food, or whose bellies are not easy of passage: for all these it is beneficial to eat many times a day, to make use of all kinds of foods [208] and of relishes prepared in every manner, and to drink two or three wines.
But those who do not vomit up their food, or who also have moist bellies: for all these it is beneficial to do the opposite of this manner.
It is suitable to vomit up food for those who wish either to cleanse out the belly or to make a moderate evacuation of the whole.
He thinks it right that these should eat often and eat varied things, and drink several wines.
Conversely, those who do not wish to vomit and who have bellies moister than is proper, so as to require checking, should neither eat often nor take foods and wines of many kinds.

For eating once some single uniform thing and drinking one wine contributes to the stomach's retaining them and concocting them, whereas the opposite things are both harder to concoct and harder to remain in the stomach.

beads.greek: παρὰ δὲ τὴν ποιότητα τῶν προσενηνεγμένων καὶ [209] τὴν τάξιν τῆς προσφορᾶς, ἤτοι γ᾿ ἐπιπολάζειν αὐτὰ, ἢ ὑπέρ- χεσθαι κάτω συμβαίνει.
beads.english: But depending on the quality of what has been taken in and [209] the order of the administration, it happens that these either float on the surface or pass down below.

beads.greek: Τὰ δὲ παιδία χρὴ τὰ νήπια βρέχειν ἐν θερμῷ ὕδατι που- λὺν χρόνον καὶ πίνειν ὑδαρέστατον τὸν οἶνον διδόναι καὶ μὴ ψυχρὸν παντάπασι.
beads.english: Infant children should be bathed in warm water for a long time, and should be given wine to drink that is very watery and not entirely cold.

beads.greek: τοῦτον δὲ διδόναι, ὃς ἥκι- στα τὴν γαστέρα μετεωρέει καὶ φῦσαν παρέξει.
beads.english: And one should give that wine which least distends the belly and will produce flatus.

beads.greek: ταῦτα δὲ ποιέειν, ὅκως οἴ τε σπασμοὶ ἧσσον ἐπιλαμβάνωσιν καὶ μείζονα γίνηται καὶ εὐχροώτερα.
beads.english: These things are to be done so that convulsions may seize them less, and they may grow larger and be of better colour.

beads.greek: Αὐτὸς εἶπε τοὺς σκοποὺς τῆς εἰρημένης διαίτης. ἵνα γὰρ οἵ τε σπασμοὶ ἧσσον ἐπιλαμβάνωσι καὶ μείζοα γίγνηται καὶ εὐχροώτερα.
beads.english: He himself has stated the aims of the regimen described: namely, that convulsions may seize them less and that they may grow larger and be of better colour.

beads.greek: τὰ γὰρ ἐν ὕδατι θερμῷ βρεχό- μενα παιδία πλείονι χρόνῳ μαλακὰ διαμένει, τοῦτο δ᾿ εἰς τὸ μὴ σπᾶσθαι συντελεῖ.
beads.english: For children who are bathed in warm water remain soft for a longer time, and this contributes to their not being convulsed.

greek_sentences: παρὰ δὲ τὴν ποιότητα τῶν προσενηνεγμένων καὶ [209] τὴν τάξιν τῆς προσφορᾶς, ἤτοι γ᾿ ἐπιπολάζειν αὐτὰ, ἢ ὑπέρ- χεσθαι κάτω συμβαίνει.
Τὰ δὲ παιδία χρὴ τὰ νήπια βρέχειν ἐν θερμῷ ὕδατι που- λὺν χρόνον καὶ πίνειν ὑδαρέστατον τὸν οἶνον διδόναι καὶ μὴ ψυχρὸν παντάπασι.
τοῦτον δὲ διδόναι, ὃς ἥκι- στα τὴν γαστέρα μετεωρέει καὶ φῦσαν παρέξει.
ταῦτα δὲ ποιέειν, ὅκως οἴ τε σπασμοὶ ἧσσον ἐπιλαμβάνωσιν καὶ μείζονα γίνηται καὶ εὐχροώτερα.
Αὐτὸς εἶπε τοὺς σκοποὺς τῆς εἰρημένης διαίτης.
ἵνα γὰρ οἵ τε σπασμοὶ ἧσσον ἐπιλαμβάνωσι καὶ μείζοα γίγνηται καὶ εὐχροώτερα.
τὰ γὰρ ἐν ὕδατι θερμῷ βρεχό- μενα παιδία πλείονι χρόνῳ μαλακὰ διαμένει, τοῦτο δ᾿ εἰς τὸ μὴ σπᾶσθαι συντελεῖ.
english_sentences: But depending on the quality of what has been taken in and [209] the order of the administration, it happens that these either float on the surface or pass down below.
Infant children should be bathed in warm water for a long time, and should be given wine to drink that is very watery and not entirely cold.
And one should give that wine which least distends the belly and will produce flatus.
These things are to be done so that convulsions may seize them less, and they may grow larger and be of better colour.
He himself has stated the aims of the regimen described: namely, that convulsions may seize them less and that they may grow larger and be of better colour.
For children who are bathed in warm water remain soft for a longer time, and this contributes to their not being convulsed.

beads.greek: τοὺς γὰρ σπασμοὺς αὐτὸς ὁ Ἱπ- ποκράτης τοῖς ἐντεταμένοις σώμασι μᾶλλον γίγνεσθαί φησι τῶν ἀνιεμένων καὶ χαλαρῶν, αὔξεται δὲ τὰ μαλακὰ σώματα [210] ῥᾷον, ἐπειδὴ καὶ πάντη τὴν διάστασιν εὐκολωτέραν ἴσχῃ.
beads.english: For Hippocrates himself says that convulsions occur more in bodies that are tense than in those that are relaxed and slack; and soft bodies [210] grow more easily, since they also have an easier expansion in every direction.

beads.greek: ὅτι δὲ τὰ μήτε σπασμοῖς ἁλισκόμενα καὶ καλῶς αὐξανόμενα τὴν ὅλην ἕξιν ὑγιεινὴν ἴσχει πρόδηλον παντί.
beads.english: That those which are neither seized by convulsions and grow well have their whole condition healthy is evident to everyone.

beads.greek: τοῦτ᾿ οὖν αὐτῷ δεδήλωται δι᾿ ἑνὸς γνωρίσματος οὐ μικροῦ τῆς εὐχροίας.
beads.english: This, then, he has indicated through one sign, and that no small one, namely good colour.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οἶνον ὑδαρῆ κελεύει πίνειν αὐτὰ, μὴ βουλό- μενος ὑπερθερμαίνεσθαι καὶ μάλιστα διὰ τὸ σπᾶσθαι πολ- λάκις αὐτὰ, ὃ πάλιν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὴν τῶν νεύρων ἀσθένειαν γίνεται καὶ τὴν ἀδηφαγίαν.
beads.english: But he also orders them to drink their wine watery, not wishing them to be overheated, and especially because they are often convulsed, which again happens to them through the weakness of the nerves and through voracity.

beads.greek: διὰ τοῦτ᾿ οὖν αὐτὸς καὶ μὴ ψυχρὸν αὐτὰ πίνειν κελεύει.
beads.english: For this reason, then, he himself also orders them not to drink it cold.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον δεῖν εἶναι τὸν οἶνον, ὃς ἥκιστα φυσώδης ἐστὶν, ἅπασι κοινῇ συμφέρει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς νηπίοις.
beads.english: That the wine must be of such a kind as is least flatulent is beneficial to all human beings in common, not only to infants.

beads.greek: Τὰς δὲ γυναῖκας ὧδε χρὴ διαιτᾶσθαι τῷ ξηροτέρῳ τρόπῳ.
beads.english: Women ought to be dieted thus, in the drier manner.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ τὰ ξηρὰ σιτία ἐπιτηδειότερα πρὸς τὴν μαλθακό- τητα τῶν γυναικείων σαρκῶν καὶ τὰ πόματα ἀκρητέστερα ἀμείνω πρὸς τὰς ὑστέρας καὶ τὰς κυητροφίας.
beads.english: For dry foods are more suited to the softness of women's flesh, and less diluted drinks are better for the wombs and for the nourishing of the foetus.

greek_sentences: τοὺς γὰρ σπασμοὺς αὐτὸς ὁ Ἱπ- ποκράτης τοῖς ἐντεταμένοις σώμασι μᾶλλον γίγνεσθαί φησι τῶν ἀνιεμένων καὶ χαλαρῶν, αὔξεται δὲ τὰ μαλακὰ σώματα [210] ῥᾷον, ἐπειδὴ καὶ πάντη τὴν διάστασιν εὐκολωτέραν ἴσχῃ.
ὅτι δὲ τὰ μήτε σπασμοῖς ἁλισκόμενα καὶ καλῶς αὐξανόμενα τὴν ὅλην ἕξιν ὑγιεινὴν ἴσχει πρόδηλον παντί.
τοῦτ᾿ οὖν αὐτῷ δεδήλωται δι᾿ ἑνὸς γνωρίσματος οὐ μικροῦ τῆς εὐχροίας.
ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οἶνον ὑδαρῆ κελεύει πίνειν αὐτὰ, μὴ βουλό- μενος ὑπερθερμαίνεσθαι καὶ μάλιστα διὰ τὸ σπᾶσθαι πολ- λάκις αὐτὰ, ὃ πάλιν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὴν τῶν νεύρων ἀσθένειαν γίνεται καὶ τὴν ἀδηφαγίαν.
διὰ τοῦτ᾿ οὖν αὐτὸς καὶ μὴ ψυχρὸν αὐτὰ πίνειν κελεύει.
τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον δεῖν εἶναι τὸν οἶνον, ὃς ἥκιστα φυσώδης ἐστὶν, ἅπασι κοινῇ συμφέρει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς νηπίοις.
Τὰς δὲ γυναῖκας ὧδε χρὴ διαιτᾶσθαι τῷ ξηροτέρῳ τρόπῳ.
καὶ γὰρ τὰ ξηρὰ σιτία ἐπιτηδειότερα πρὸς τὴν μαλθακό- τητα τῶν γυναικείων σαρκῶν καὶ τὰ πόματα ἀκρητέστερα ἀμείνω πρὸς τὰς ὑστέρας καὶ τὰς κυητροφίας.
english_sentences: For Hippocrates himself says that convulsions occur more in bodies that are tense than in those that are relaxed and slack; and soft bodies [210] grow more easily, since they also have an easier expansion in every direction.
That those which are neither seized by convulsions and grow well have their whole condition healthy is evident to everyone.
This, then, he has indicated through one sign, and that no small one, namely good colour.

But he also orders them to drink their wine watery, not wishing them to be overheated, and especially because they are often convulsed, which again happens to them through the weakness of the nerves and through voracity.
For this reason, then, he himself also orders them not to drink it cold.
That the wine must be of such a kind as is least flatulent is beneficial to all human beings in common, not only to infants.
Women ought to be dieted thus, in the drier manner.
For dry foods are more suited to the softness of women's flesh, and less diluted drinks are better for the wombs and for the nourishing of the foetus.

beads.greek: [211] Τὰς γυναῖκας ἀξιώσας διαιτᾶσθαι τῷ ξηροτέρῳ τρόπῳ, ὁποῖός τέ ἐστιν οὗτος αὐτὸς ὑπέγραψεν.
beads.english: [211] Having required that women follow a regimen of the drier manner, he has himself also outlined what sort of manner this is.

beads.greek: ἔχει δὲ ἀντιλο- γίαν ἡ δόξα τἀνδρός.
beads.english: But the man's opinion is open to objection.

beads.greek: εἰ μὲν γὰρ παρὰ φύσιν ἦν ταῖς γυ- ναιξὶν ὑγραῖς εἶναι, καθάπερ ἐπί τε τῶν δυσκράτων φύσεων καὶ τῶν νοσούντων ὑγρὸν νόσημα, καλῶς ἂν αὐτὰς ἐξήρα- νεν· ἐπειδὴ δὲ τοῦτο κατὰ φύσιν αὐταῖς ἐστι, φυλάττειν αὐτὸ χρὴ, πλὴν εἰ τὴν ὑγιεινήν ποτε συμμετρίαν ὑπερβαίη.
beads.english: For if it were contrary to nature for women to be moist, as is the case with ill-tempered natures and with those suffering from a moist disease, he would rightly have dried them; but since this is according to nature for them, one ought to preserve it, unless it should at some time exceed the healthy proportion.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ τοῦτό γε κᾀπὶ τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐσκοπούμεθα.
beads.english: But this, at least, we consider in the case of men as well.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ καὶ τούτοις ξηροτέροις μὲν εἶναι τῶν γυναικῶν κατὰ φύσιν ἐστίν. ἐπειδὰν δὲ τῆς προσηκούσης ξηρότητος ἐπὶ πλέον προέλθωσι, τότ᾿ αὐτῶν τὴν δυσκρασίαν ἐπανορθούμεθα διὰ τῶν ἐναντίων.
beads.english: For it is according to nature for them too to be drier than women; but whenever they advance further than the appropriate dryness, then we correct their dyscrasia by means of the opposites.

beads.greek: Τοὺς γυμναζομένους χρὴ χειμῶνος καὶ τρέχειν καὶ παλαίειν, τοῦ θέρεος παλαίειν μὲν ὀλίγα, τρέχειν δὲ μὴ, περιπα- τέειν δὲ πολλὰ κατὰ ψῦχος.
beads.english: Those who take exercise ought in winter both to run and to wrestle; in summer to wrestle only a little and not to run, but to walk a great deal in the cool.

greek_sentences: [211] Τὰς γυναῖκας ἀξιώσας διαιτᾶσθαι τῷ ξηροτέρῳ τρόπῳ, ὁποῖός τέ ἐστιν οὗτος αὐτὸς ὑπέγραψεν.
ἔχει δὲ ἀντιλο- γίαν ἡ δόξα τἀνδρός.

εἰ μὲν γὰρ παρὰ φύσιν ἦν ταῖς γυ- ναιξὶν ὑγραῖς εἶναι, καθάπερ ἐπί τε τῶν δυσκράτων φύσεων καὶ τῶν νοσούντων ὑγρὸν νόσημα, καλῶς ἂν αὐτὰς ἐξήρα- νεν· ἐπειδὴ δὲ τοῦτο κατὰ φύσιν αὐταῖς ἐστι, φυλάττειν αὐτὸ χρὴ, πλὴν εἰ τὴν ὑγιεινήν ποτε συμμετρίαν ὑπερβαίη.
ἀλλὰ τοῦτό γε κᾀπὶ τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐσκοπούμεθα.
καὶ γὰρ καὶ τούτοις ξηροτέροις μὲν εἶναι τῶν γυναικῶν κατὰ φύσιν ἐστίν.
ἐπειδὰν δὲ τῆς προσηκούσης ξηρότητος ἐπὶ πλέον προέλθωσι, τότ᾿ αὐτῶν τὴν δυσκρασίαν ἐπανορθούμεθα διὰ τῶν ἐναντίων.
Τοὺς γυμναζομένους χρὴ χειμῶνος καὶ τρέχειν καὶ παλαίειν, τοῦ θέρεος παλαίειν μὲν ὀλίγα, τρέχειν δὲ μὴ, περιπα- τέειν δὲ πολλὰ κατὰ ψῦχος.
english_sentences: [211] Having required that women follow a regimen of the drier manner, he has himself also outlined what sort of manner this is.
But the man's opinion is open to objection.

For if it were contrary to nature for women to be moist, as is the case with ill-tempered natures and with those suffering from a moist disease, he would rightly have dried them; but since this is according to nature for them, one ought to preserve it, unless it should at some time exceed the healthy proportion.
But this, at least, we consider in the case of men as well.
For it is according to nature for them too to be drier than women; but whenever they advance further than the appropriate dryness, then we correct their dyscrasia by means of the opposites.
Those who take exercise ought in winter both to run and to wrestle; in summer to wrestle only a little and not to run, but to walk a great deal in the cool.

beads.greek: [212] Γυμνασίων διαφορὰς οἰκείων ταῖς ὥραις διδάσκει, τοῦ μὲν χειμῶνος θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν δυναμένων, τοῦ δὲ θέρους ἔμπαλιν.
beads.english: [212] He teaches the differences among exercises that suit the seasons: in winter, those able to heat and dry; in summer, the opposite.

beads.greek: Ὁκόσοι κοπιῶσιν ἐκ τῶν δρόμων, τουτέους παλαίειν χρή. ὁκόσοι δ᾿ ἂν παλαίοντες κοπιῶσι, τουτέους χρὴ τρέχειν.
beads.english: Those who become fatigued from running should wrestle, and those who become fatigued while wrestling should run.

beads.greek: οὕτω γὰρ ἂν ὁ ταλαιπωρέων τῷ κοπιῶντι τοῦ σώματος διαθερμαίνοιτο καὶ συνιστοῖτο καὶ διαναπαύοιτο μάλιστα.
beads.english: For in this way the one who is exerting himself would, in the fatigued part of the body, be best warmed through, braced, and given rest.

beads.greek: Εἰ οὕτως ἐγέγραπτο πάντα τοῖς δογματικοῖς ἰα- τροῖς, οὐκ ἂν εἶχον ἀφορμὴν πολυλογίας οἱ ἐξηγηταί.
beads.english: If everything had been written in this way by the dogmatic physicians, the commentators would have had no occasion for verbosity.

beads.greek: λέγω δ᾿ οὕτως ὡς προσθεῖναι τὴν αἰτίαν, δι᾿ ἣν ὧδέ πως ἐκέ- λευσε πράττειν ἡμᾶς, ὅπερ νῦν ἐποίησεν ὁ Πόλυβος.
beads.english: By 'in this way' I mean adding the reason for which he ordered us to act thus, which is exactly what Polybus has now done.

greek_sentences: [212] Γυμνασίων διαφορὰς οἰκείων ταῖς ὥραις διδάσκει, τοῦ μὲν χειμῶνος θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν δυναμένων, τοῦ δὲ θέρους ἔμπαλιν.
Ὁκόσοι κοπιῶσιν ἐκ τῶν δρόμων, τουτέους παλαίειν χρή.
ὁκόσοι δ᾿ ἂν παλαίοντες κοπιῶσι, τουτέους χρὴ τρέχειν.
οὕτω γὰρ ἂν ὁ ταλαιπωρέων τῷ κοπιῶντι τοῦ σώματος διαθερμαίνοιτο καὶ συνιστοῖτο καὶ διαναπαύοιτο μάλιστα.
Εἰ οὕτως ἐγέγραπτο πάντα τοῖς δογματικοῖς ἰα- τροῖς, οὐκ ἂν εἶχον ἀφορμὴν πολυλογίας οἱ ἐξηγηταί.
λέγω δ᾿ οὕτως ὡς προσθεῖναι τὴν αἰτίαν, δι᾿ ἣν ὧδέ πως ἐκέ- λευσε πράττειν ἡμᾶς, ὅπερ νῦν ἐποίησεν ὁ Πόλυβος.
english_sentences: [212] He teaches the differences among exercises that suit the seasons: in winter, those able to heat and dry; in summer, the opposite.
Those who become fatigued from running should wrestle, and those who become fatigued while wrestling should run.
For in this way the one who is exerting himself would, in the fatigued part of the body, be best warmed through, braced, and given rest.
If everything had been written in this way by the dogmatic physicians, the commentators would have had no occasion for verbosity.
By 'in this way' I mean adding the reason for which he ordered us to act thus, which is exactly what Polybus has now done.

beads.greek: Ὁκόσους γυμναζομένους μάλιστα διάῤῥοιαι λαμβάνουσι καὶ τὰ ὑποχωρήματα σιτώδεα καὶ ἄπεπτα, τουτέοισι τῶν τε [213] γυμνασίων ἀφαιρέειν, μὴ ἔλασσον τοῦ τρίτου μέρους καὶ τῶν σιτίων τοῖσιν ἡμίσεσι χρέεσθαι.
beads.english: Those who, while exercising, are especially seized by diarrhoeas, and whose evacuations are food-like (σιτώδεα) and unconcocted: from these one must take away some of their [213] exercises, not less than a third part, and they should use half of their foods.

beads.greek: δῆλον γὰρ δὴ ὅτι ἡ κοιλίη ξυνθάλπειν οὐ δύναται, ὥστε πέσσεσθαι τὸ πλῆ- θος τῶν εἰσιόντων σιτίων.
beads.english: For it is clear that the belly is unable to warm them thoroughly, so that the quantity of the foods entering is concocted.

beads.greek: ἔστω δὲ τουτέοισι τὰ σιτία ἄρτος ὡς ἐξοπτότατος ἐν οἴνῳ ἐντετριμμένος καὶ τὰ πό- ματα ὡς ἐλάχιστα καὶ ἀκρητέστατα, καὶ περιπάτοισι μὴ χρεέσθωσαν ἀπὸ τοῦ σιτίου.
beads.english: Let the foods for these be bread baked as thoroughly as possible, crumbled into wine, and let the drinks be as few as possible and as unmixed as possible; and let them not take walks after the meal.

beads.greek: μονοσιτέειν δὲ χρὴ ὑπὸ τοῦτον τὸν χρόνον, οὕτω γὰρ ἂν μάλιστα ξυνθάλποιτο ἡ κοιλίη καὶ τῶν εἰσιόντων ἐπικρατέοι.
beads.english: They should eat only once a day during this time, for in this way the belly would most of all be warmed thoroughly and would master what enters.

beads.greek: γίνεται δὲ ὁ τρό- πος οὗτος τῆς διαῤῥοίης τῶν σωμάτων μάλιστα τοῖσι πυ- κνοσάρκοισιν, ὁκόταν ἀναγκάζηται ὁ ἄνθρωπος κρεηφαγέειν, τῆς φύσιος ὑπαρχούσης τοιαύτης.
beads.english: This kind of diarrhoea of bodies occurs especially in those of dense flesh, whenever the person is compelled to eat meat while his nature is of this kind.

beads.greek: αἱ γὰρ φλέβες πυκνω- θεῖσαι οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων τῶν εἰσιόντων.
beads.english: For the veins, having been made dense, do not take hold of the foods that enter.

greek_sentences: Ὁκόσους γυμναζομένους μάλιστα διάῤῥοιαι λαμβάνουσι καὶ τὰ ὑποχωρήματα σιτώδεα καὶ ἄπεπτα, τουτέοισι τῶν τε [213] γυμνασίων ἀφαιρέειν, μὴ ἔλασσον τοῦ τρίτου μέρους καὶ τῶν σιτίων τοῖσιν ἡμίσεσι χρέεσθαι.
δῆλον γὰρ δὴ ὅτι ἡ κοιλίη ξυνθάλπειν οὐ δύναται, ὥστε πέσσεσθαι τὸ πλῆ- θος τῶν εἰσιόντων σιτίων.
ἔστω δὲ τουτέοισι τὰ σιτία ἄρτος ὡς ἐξοπτότατος ἐν οἴνῳ ἐντετριμμένος καὶ τὰ πό- ματα ὡς ἐλάχιστα καὶ ἀκρητέστατα, καὶ περιπάτοισι μὴ χρεέσθωσαν ἀπὸ τοῦ σιτίου.
μονοσιτέειν δὲ χρὴ ὑπὸ τοῦτον τὸν χρόνον, οὕτω γὰρ ἂν μάλιστα ξυνθάλποιτο ἡ κοιλίη καὶ τῶν εἰσιόντων ἐπικρατέοι.
γίνεται δὲ ὁ τρό- πος οὗτος τῆς διαῤῥοίης τῶν σωμάτων μάλιστα τοῖσι πυ- κνοσάρκοισιν, ὁκόταν ἀναγκάζηται ὁ ἄνθρωπος κρεηφαγέειν, τῆς φύσιος ὑπαρχούσης τοιαύτης.
αἱ γὰρ φλέβες πυκνω- θεῖσαι οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων τῶν εἰσιόντων.
english_sentences: Those who, while exercising, are especially seized by diarrhoeas, and whose evacuations are food-like (σιτώδεα) and unconcocted: from these one must take away some of their [213] exercises, not less than a third part, and they should use half of their foods.
For it is clear that the belly is unable to warm them thoroughly, so that the quantity of the foods entering is concocted.
Let the foods for these be bread baked as thoroughly as possible, crumbled into wine, and let the drinks be as few as possible and as unmixed as possible; and let them not take walks after the meal.
They should eat only once a day during this time, for in this way the belly would most of all be warmed thoroughly and would master what enters.
This kind of diarrhoea of bodies occurs especially in those of dense flesh, whenever the person is compelled to eat meat while his nature is of this kind.
For the veins, having been made dense, do not take hold of the foods that enter.

beads.greek: Οὐ περὶ τῶν τῆς ὑγείας ἕνεκα γυμναζομένων ἔοικε ποιεῖσθαι τὸν λόγον νῦν, ἀλλὰ περὶ τῶν γυμναστικῶν τι μετιόντων ἐπιτηδευμάτων καὶ μήτε παύεσθαι τελέως αὐ- τοῦ δυναμένων μήτε εἰς πάνυ βραχὺ συστεῖλαι, διὰ τοῦτο [214] αὐτῶν ἀφαιρεῖ τοῦ μὲν γυμνασίου τὸ τρίτον μέρος, τῶν δὲ σιτίων τὸ ἥμισυ.
beads.english: He seems to be making his discourse now not about those who exercise for the sake of health, but about those who pursue some one of the gymnastic practices and are able neither to stop it entirely nor to reduce it to a very small amount; for this reason [214] he removes from them a third part of the exercise and half of the food.

beads.greek: τοσοῦτο γὰρ ἐλπίζει κρατήσειν αὐτοῦ, ὡς μηκέτι ἀπεπτεῖν τε καὶ διαῤῥοΐζεσθαι.
beads.english: For by so much he hopes to get the better of it, so that they no longer fail to digest and suffer diarrhoea.

beads.greek: ὀρθῶς δ᾿ ἐποίη- σε κᾀνταῦθα προσγράψας αὐτῶν τὸν λογισμὸν, ᾦ χρώμενος αὐτά τε ταῦτα καὶ τὰ τούτοις εἰρημένα συνεβούλευσε.
beads.english: He did rightly here too in adding his reasoning about them, using which he advised both these very things and those stated together with them.

beads.greek: γίνε- ται γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ τρόπος οὗτος τῆς διαῤῥοΐης τοῖσι πυκνο- σάρκοισι, ὅταν κρεηφαγεῖν ἀναγκάζωνται, δηλώσας ἐνταῦθα περὶ τῶν γυμναστικῶν εἶναι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ.
beads.english: For this type of diarrhoea, he says, occurs in those of dense flesh when they are compelled to eat meat; by this he made clear that his discourse here concerns the athletes, for it is these whom they compel to eat meat.

beads.greek: κρεηφαγεῖν γὰρ ἀναγκάζουσι τούτους· εἶτ᾿ ἐφεξῆς φησιν, αἱ φλέβες πυ- κνωθεῖσαι οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων τῶν εἰσιόντων.
beads.english: Then next he says: the veins, having been condensed, do not take hold of the food that enters.

beads.greek: ἀσαφῶς δὲ εἶπε τοῦτο καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἠναγκάσθησαν ὑπολα- βεῖν οἱ ἐξηγηταὶ τὸ τὰς πυκνωθείσας αὐτὸν λέγειν, ἀντὶ τοῦ σκληρὰς γινομένας καὶ δυσεπεκτάτους, ὡς μὴ παραδέ- χεσθαι τὴν τροφὴν καὶ σημαίνεσθαι τοῦτό φασιν, ἐκ τοῦ οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων, ἀλλὰ τοῦτό γε τὴν ἀνάδο- σιν μᾶλλον, οὐ τὴν πέψιν εἴωθε βλάπτειν, ὥστε διαχωρεῖν μὲν αὐτοὺς ὑγρὰ, οὐ μὴν ἄπεπτα.
beads.english: He said this unclearly, and for this reason the exegetes were compelled to suppose that by 'condensed' he means veins that are becoming hard and difficult to distend, so as not to receive the nourishment; and they say that this is what is signified by 'they do not take hold of the food'. But this, at any rate, is wont to harm the distribution rather than the digestion, so that such people pass fluid stools, yet not undigested ones.

beads.greek: προείρηται δὲ ὑπ᾿ αὐ- τοῦ σιτώδη καὶ ἄπεπτα τοὺς τοιούτους διαχωρεῖν.
beads.english: Yet it has been said before by him that such people pass food-like and undigested stools.

greek_sentences: Οὐ περὶ τῶν τῆς ὑγείας ἕνεκα γυμναζομένων ἔοικε ποιεῖσθαι τὸν λόγον νῦν, ἀλλὰ περὶ τῶν γυμναστικῶν τι μετιόντων ἐπιτηδευμάτων καὶ μήτε παύεσθαι τελέως αὐ- τοῦ δυναμένων μήτε εἰς πάνυ βραχὺ συστεῖλαι, διὰ τοῦτο [214] αὐτῶν ἀφαιρεῖ τοῦ μὲν γυμνασίου τὸ τρίτον μέρος, τῶν δὲ σιτίων τὸ ἥμισυ.
τοσοῦτο γὰρ ἐλπίζει κρατήσειν αὐτοῦ, ὡς μηκέτι ἀπεπτεῖν τε καὶ διαῤῥοΐζεσθαι.
ὀρθῶς δ᾿ ἐποίη- σε κᾀνταῦθα προσγράψας αὐτῶν τὸν λογισμὸν, ᾦ χρώμενος αὐτά τε ταῦτα καὶ τὰ τούτοις εἰρημένα συνεβούλευσε.
γίνε- ται γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ τρόπος οὗτος τῆς διαῤῥοΐης τοῖσι πυκνο- σάρκοισι, ὅταν κρεηφαγεῖν ἀναγκάζωνται, δηλώσας ἐνταῦθα περὶ τῶν γυμναστικῶν εἶναι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ.
κρεηφαγεῖν γὰρ ἀναγκάζουσι τούτους· εἶτ᾿ ἐφεξῆς φησιν, αἱ φλέβες πυ- κνωθεῖσαι οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων τῶν εἰσιόντων.

ἀσαφῶς δὲ εἶπε τοῦτο καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἠναγκάσθησαν ὑπολα- βεῖν οἱ ἐξηγηταὶ τὸ τὰς πυκνωθείσας αὐτὸν λέγειν, ἀντὶ τοῦ σκληρὰς γινομένας καὶ δυσεπεκτάτους, ὡς μὴ παραδέ- χεσθαι τὴν τροφὴν καὶ σημαίνεσθαι τοῦτό φασιν, ἐκ τοῦ οὐκ ἀντιλαμβάνονται τῶν σιτίων, ἀλλὰ τοῦτό γε τὴν ἀνάδο- σιν μᾶλλον, οὐ τὴν πέψιν εἴωθε βλάπτειν, ὥστε διαχωρεῖν μὲν αὐτοὺς ὑγρὰ, οὐ μὴν ἄπεπτα.
προείρηται δὲ ὑπ᾿ αὐ- τοῦ σιτώδη καὶ ἄπεπτα τοὺς τοιούτους διαχωρεῖν.
english_sentences: He seems to be making his discourse now not about those who exercise for the sake of health, but about those who pursue some one of the gymnastic practices and are able neither to stop it entirely nor to reduce it to a very small amount; for this reason [214] he removes from them a third part of the exercise and half of the food.
For by so much he hopes to get the better of it, so that they no longer fail to digest and suffer diarrhoea.
He did rightly here too in adding his reasoning about them, using which he advised both these very things and those stated together with them.

For this type of diarrhoea, he says, occurs in those of dense flesh when they are compelled to eat meat; by this he made clear that his discourse here concerns the athletes, for it is these whom they compel to eat meat.
Then next he says: the veins, having been condensed, do not take hold of the food that enters.

He said this unclearly, and for this reason the exegetes were compelled to suppose that by 'condensed' he means veins that are becoming hard and difficult to distend, so as not to receive the nourishment; and they say that this is what is signified by 'they do not take hold of the food'.
But this, at any rate, is wont to harm the distribution rather than the digestion, so that such people pass fluid stools, yet not undigested ones.
Yet it has been said before by him that such people pass food-like and undigested stools.

beads.greek: ὁπόταν δὲ προσγράψαντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λογισμὸν, ᾧ πιστεύσας συνε- [215] βούλευσεν ἅ συνεβούλευσεν, ὅμως ἀπορία τις ὑπολείπεται, τί χρὴ νομίζειν γίνεσθαι κατ᾿ ἐκείνους τῶν λόγων, ἐν οἷς οὐ προσέγραψε τὴν αἰτίαν ὧν κελεύει ποιεῖν ἡμᾶς.
beads.english: When, then, even though he has added the reasoning in reliance on which he advised [215] what he advised, some difficulty nevertheless remains, what must one suppose happens in those passages of his text in which he did not add the cause of the things he bids us do?

beads.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ εἰ μὲν μὴ προσεγεγράφει περὶ τῶν πυκνοσάρκων, ὡμολόγουν ἂν ἀπορεῖν παντάπασιν ὡς ἐπὶ πολλῶν ἄλλων, ἐν οἷς οὐδὲν τοιοῦτον προστεθέντος τοῦ συγγραφέως ἀποφαίνονται τολ- μηρότατοι τὸ ἐπελθὸν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἐξηγηταί.
beads.english: For my part, had he not added the words about those of dense flesh, I would admit that I was entirely at a loss, as in many other cases in which, though the author has added nothing of the sort, the exegetes with the greatest boldness declare whatever comes into their heads.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ δὲ αὐτὸς ἐμνημόνευσε τῶν πυκνοσάρκων, ἀφορμὴν ἔδωκε τοῦ γράψαι τι καὶ αὐτοὺς χρήσιμον ἐπὶ τῶν τοιούτων φύσεων.
beads.english: But since he himself made mention of those of dense flesh, he has given an occasion for us too to write something useful concerning such natures.

beads.greek: ἀθροίζουσι γὰρ οὗτοι τάχιστα πλῆθος, ἐλλιπῶς διαπνεόμε- νοι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀναδόσεως ἰσχομένης αὐτοῖς, ὑγρὰ μὲν πάντως γίνεται τὰ διαχωρήματα, ποτὲ δ᾿ οὐχ ὑγρὰ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ λεπτὰ καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῶν ἀδηφαγούντων.
beads.english: For these people very quickly accumulate a plethora, since they transpire deficiently; and because the distribution is for this reason held back in them, their excretions are in every case fluid, and sometimes not only fluid but also thin, especially in those who eat voraciously.

beads.greek: ὅταν μὲν γὰρ ἀναδίδοταί τι τῶν καταποθέντων, ἑτοιμότερον ἡ γαστὴρ πέττει τὰ κατάλοιπα. διαμένοντος δὲ ἐν αὐτῇ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν σιτίων, ὅταν ποτὲ βαρύνηται πρὸς αὐτῶν, ἀποτρίβεται πάντα πρὶν πεφθῆναι.
beads.english: For when some part of what has been swallowed is distributed, the stomach concocts what remains more readily; but when the mass of food stays on in it, then, whenever it is weighed down by it, it throws everything off before it has been concocted.

greek_sentences: ὁπόταν δὲ προσγράψαντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λογισμὸν, ᾧ πιστεύσας συνε- [215] βούλευσεν ἅ συνεβούλευσεν, ὅμως ἀπορία τις ὑπολείπεται, τί χρὴ νομίζειν γίνεσθαι κατ᾿ ἐκείνους τῶν λόγων, ἐν οἷς οὐ προσέγραψε τὴν αἰτίαν ὧν κελεύει ποιεῖν ἡμᾶς.
